label: Tête de Moine
note: Eaten as thin rosettes shaved with the girolle (invented 1982 by Nicolas Crevoisier); AOC 2001, AOP since 2010

about.text: Tête de Moine is a semi-hard Swiss cheese from raw cow milk, made in the Bernese Jura and Canton of Jura and pared into rosettes rather than cut.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.
shaved into rosettes with a girolle

facts.v: Processed in copper vats, within 24 h of the oldest milking
At least 120 days of green feeding; no silage
